blocks.text: At the Chau Chak Wing Museum in Sydney, Nigerian artist Victor Ehikhamenor’s first Australian solo exhibition, ‘Undoing the City: Making Home’, examines how communities preserve their histories and identities amid urban transformation.

At the Chau Chak Wing Museum in Sydney, Australia, Nigerian artist Victor Ehikhamenor’s first Australian solo exhibition, Undoing the City: Making Home, examines how communities preserve their histories and identities amid urban transformation.

What happens to a community’s identity when the places that hold its memories disappear? In ‘Undoing the City: Making Home’, Nigerian artist Victor Ehikhamenor explores the human consequences of urban redevelopment, displacement and the struggle to preserve cultural belonging. The exhibition brings together new and recent works connecting the experiences of communities in Sydney, Cairo and Port Harcourt. Drawing on research into neighbourhoods threatened by redevelopment, Ehikhamenor examines how architecture, collective memory and cultural practices shape our understanding of home.
Informed by the visual and spiritual traditions of the historic Benin Kingdom, his multidisciplinary practice engages with colonial histories, identity and the relationship between people and place.

Presented in partnership with Blacktown Arts, the exhibition also extends beyond the museum through a mentorship programme supporting emerging African and African-descended creatives in Western Sydney. By placing geographically distinct communities in conversation, Undoing the City: Making Home asks whose histories survive urban transformation and how artistic practice can resist erasure.
The exhibition invites audiences to reconsider home not simply as a physical location, but as a repository of relationships, histories and cultural continuity.
This exhibition will be on view at the Penelope Gallery, the Chau Chak Wing Museum , University of Sydney, from 15 October 2026 to 26 April 2027.
